name: Android
summary: Google's open-source mobile operating system (AOSP), shipped on devices by many manufacturers, whose security fixes are published in a monthly bulletin and delivered as security patch levels.
package_manager: System updates from the device maker; Google Play system updates
patch_notes: Fixes listed in the bulletin come from AOSP, the upstream Linux kernel, and chipset makers. A device is covered once its security patch level is at or after the bulletin's level (for example 2026-11-05 for the November 2026 bulletin); when and whether a device gets that level is up to its manufacturer.
advisory_notes: Bulletins are published on the first Monday of each month (the next work day when that Monday is a holiday), each with two patch levels, YYYY-MM-01 and YYYY-MM-05. Each issue carries a CVE and an Android bug ID (A-) and lists the updated AOSP versions; the November 2026 bulletin listed 14, 15, 16, 16-qpr2, and 17. Device and chipset makers publish their own bulletins too.

identify.command: Settings > About phone (or About tablet) > Android version
identify.shows: Android version, Android security update (the patch level), Google Play system update, and build number

identify_basis: From Google's Check and update your Android version help page.
licence: The Android Open Source Project is open source; device builds add the maker's own components.

name: FreeRTOS
summary: An open-source real-time kernel for microcontrollers, maintained with Amazon Web Services, with long-term support (LTS) libraries.
package_manager: None; the kernel is compiled into the device firmware
patch_notes: Firmware picks up a fix by moving to a fixed FreeRTOS-Kernel release and rebuilding; the latest release when this page was built was V11.3.3.
advisory_notes: Advisories are published as GitHub Security Advisories on the kernel repository; reports go to the AWS vulnerability reporting page or aws-security@amazon.com.
identify_basis: No identify command is listed: FreeRTOS has no shell. The kernel version is set at build time in the firmware's source tree.

eol.note: The FreeRTOS LTS page loads its support periods with scripts, so no dates were confirmed; open it in a browser.

licence: Free and open source; see the LICENSE file in the FreeRTOS-Kernel repository.

name: Zephyr RTOS
summary: An open-source real-time operating system for microcontrollers, with releases every six months and a long-term support (LTS) release for products.
package_manager: None; Zephyr is source code built into the firmware with West
patch_notes: Major releases come every six months (April and October) and stable releases are supported for two release cycles, about a year; LTS releases are maintained for at least five years.
advisory_notes: The vulnerabilities page lists each CVE by year, and details can follow once an embargo lifts.
identify_basis: No identify command is listed: the Zephyr version is set at build time in the firmware's source tree (West manifest).

eol.note: Release and end-of-life dates from the Zephyr releases page; Zephyr publishes no separate full-support date.

licence: Free and open source; see the LICENSE file in the Zephyr repository.

name: OpenWrt
summary: An open-source Linux distribution for routers and other embedded network devices.
package_manager: `apk` or `opkg` (both packages are in the 24.10 and 25.12 source trees)
patch_notes: OpenWrt's security policy says a release series stops getting security fixes once it reaches end of life, recommends the latest minor release or a recent snapshot, and notes that not every security fix gets a CVE or advisory. Firmware upgrades use sysupgrade images from downloads.openwrt.org.
advisory_notes: openwrt.org answered automated requests with a bot check when this page was built, so open the advisory list in a browser; the GitHub security policy and the release downloads were reachable.

identify.shows: DISTRIB_RELEASE, DISTRIB_TARGET, and DISTRIB_ARCH for the running firmware
os-release fields plus OPENWRT_BOARD, OPENWRT_ARCH, and OPENWRT_RELEASE

identify_basis: From the OpenWrt source tree (package/base-files templates for both files); not run on a device for this page.
licence: Free and open source; see the LICENSE file in the OpenWrt repository.
